overview: Shandong Gold Mining is a Chinese state-controlled gold producer, dual-listed as H shares in Hong Kong (1787.HK) and A shares in Shanghai (600547.SH), and controlled by Shandong Gold Group (a Shandong provincial SOE). The Company explores, mines, processes and smelts gold (plus associated silver, lead, zinc and copper) across 13+ mines concentrated in Shandong's Jiaodong Peninsula (the world's third-largest gold-rich district) and other Chinese provinces, with a growing overseas base in Argentina (Veladero, 50%), Ghana (Cardinal), and Namibia (Osino's Twin Hills project, under construction). It also owns Shandong Gold Smelting, one of China's top-ten gold refiners, and holds a 28.89% stake in separately listed Shanjin International.

business_model.summary: Revenue comes from selling self-produced mined gold (highest margin, ~50% gross margin), externally purchased gold that is resold/refined through its smelting operations (near-zero margin, mostly a pass-through trading/volume business), and finished small gold bars and other non-ferrous by-products (silver, lead, zinc, copper). Self-produced gold is the profit engine; purchased/traded gold inflates reported revenue but contributes little margin.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - heavily concentrated via Shanghai Gold Exchange (64.5% of FY2025 sales) and other large bullion/trading counterparties; top 5 customers = 76.7% of sales
business_model.geographic_mix: Domestic (China) ~85.5% of FY2025 revenue; Overseas (Argentina, Ghana) ~14.3%, growing faster (+63% YoY) and at higher margin (41.3% vs 16.9% domestic)

main_competitors: China National Gold Group Gold Jewellery/Zhongjin Gold (600916.SH)
competitive_position.market_position: Ranked #2 among Chinese gold miners by both mined-gold production and net profit in 2024 (behind Zijin Mining, which is larger and more diversified into copper); #1 among listed domestic miners in gold production from Chinese mines for consecutive years. Controlling shareholder in Shanjin International (ranked 6th in production, 4th in profit among listed Chinese gold miners).

moat_factors.description: 2,054.33 tonnes attributable gold resource reserves at end-2025; flagship mines (Jiaojia, Sanshandao, Xincheng) sit in the Jiaodong Peninsula, the world's third-largest gold concentration area, giving multi-decade mine life at several assets

Shandong Gold Smelting has 1,200 t/day concentrate processing and 100t/yr gold refining capacity, a top-ten national smelter, capturing downstream value and enabling the purchased-gold trading business

SOE status (Shandong Gold Group, provincial SASAC) eases permitting, financing (SDG Finance Co., perpetual bonds) and alignment with China's gold industry policy, but also brings political/governance overhead
13 mines each producing >1 tonne/year gold; deepest large-diameter shaft in Asia (2,000m) demonstrates technical capability to keep mining depleting near-surface deposits economically
Constituent of SSE 50/180 and MSCI/FTSE/S&P indices; improving ESG ratings (Wind AA), but this is reputational rather than an economic moat

weaknesses: Thin, declining-mix purchased/traded gold revenue (41% of sales) dilutes consolidated margins and inflates top-line growth optics
Customer concentration: Shanghai Gold Exchange alone is 64.5% of FY2025 sales
Domestic mines are mature/deep (Sanshandao auxiliary shaft now at 2,000m), raising extraction costs over time versus newer, shallower overseas or competitor assets

Minority-owned complexity: many key mines held via partial stakes (e.g., Qinghai Dachaidan 26%, Veladero 50%, Jilin Banmiaozi 27.45% via Shanjin International), understating headline production/reserve figures and complicating capital allocation
Smaller and less diversified than Zijin Mining, which has copper/zinc/lithium alongside gold and a larger international M&A platform

growth_drivers: Gold price supercycle: international gold surged ~65% in 2025 (closing at $4,318/oz) directly flowing through to profit given largely unhedged production

Overseas production ramp: overseas mines grew 60.2% YoY in 2025 and a further 18% YoY in H1 2026, led by Cardinal's Namdini mine (Ghana) and Veladero (Argentina); Osino's Twin Hills project (Namibia) targeted for first production H1 2027

Exploration-led reserve replacement: RMB810m exploration spend in FY2025 added 81 tonnes of gold metal, exceeding annual depletion; 'resource first' strategy pairs organic exploration with M&A (e.g., Shanjin International's acquisition of 52.07% of Yunnan Western Mining)
Capacity expansion projects: Sanshandao 15,000 t/day expansion (approval targeted 2026), Jiaojia and Xincheng resource-integration projects progressing ahead of schedule
AI/automation and lean-management cost programs targeting lower cash cost per gram, offsetting the cost inflation from deeper, harder-to-reach ore bodies

Capital markets support: H-share placing raised HK$3.9bn in Sept 2025 (debt paydown), and the controlling shareholder has been actively increasing its stake (RMB510m completed by April 2026), signaling confidence

business.description: Flagship Jiaodong mines are mature and increasingly deep (2,000m+ shafts); must continuously out-explore depletion, and domestic mine production was flat to down in H1 2026 amid safety-driven suspensions

H1 2026 gold mine production fell 22.7% YoY as the company intensified resource-integration and safety-standardization work across Jiaojia/Xincheng/Sanshandao/Penglai, with management stating the full extent of the 2026 production impact is not yet determined
Shanghai Gold Exchange is 64.5% of sales; any disruption to that channel or exchange-traded gold mechanics is a single point of failure
Company explicitly flags that elevated gold prices have pushed global M&A asset valuations higher, raising transaction costs and complexity for further reserve acquisitions

financial.description: D/E around 100%+ per third-party data; relies on perpetual bonds (RMB507m interest expense in FY2025) and periodic equity raises (Sept 2025 H-share placing diluted SDG Group's stake from 45.36% to 44.02%) to fund expansion and deleveraging

H1 2026 booked a RMB705m fair-value loss on its 18.71% Donghai Securities stake (subsidiary SDG Capital Management); the company also runs gold futures/T+D trading books that have produced net investment losses in some periods
~16% of total assets are overseas (Argentina, Ghana, Namibia); ARS, GHS and NAD exposure versus RMB reporting currency, plus USD-denominated gold pricing

regulatory.description: New Implementation Regulations of the Mineral Resources Law and provincial green-mine rules raise compliance costs and are explicitly cited by management as impacting 2026 production via safety standardization work
New national gold tax administration rules took effect Nov 2025 (through 2027); resource tax payments already ~RMB2.0bn in FY2025 and rising with overseas subsidiary production

As a provincial SASAC-controlled SOE, leadership appointments are subject to state personnel policy (chairman Han Yaodong replaced by Wang Chenglong in July 2026 due to a rule barring concurrent posts at the parent group and listed company, not performance) — minority H-shareholders have limited influence over these decisions

macro.description: FY2025/H1 2026 saw extreme swings (international spot from a 2026 high of $5,598/oz to a low of $3,943/oz); management explicitly says further Fed policy shifts (new chair Kevin Warsh's credibility-restoration agenda) could dampen gold prices
RMB-denominated gold (Shanghai Gold Exchange AU(T+D)) underperformed international gold in H1 2026 due to RMB appreciation, directly compressing domestic realized prices versus the USD gold price

Global gold jewelry demand fell ~23% YoY in Q1 2026 and to a post-pandemic quarterly low in Q2 2026 as high/volatile prices deterred retail buyers, though this is partly offset by continued strong investment-bar/coin and central-bank demand

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold mining remains in a structurally supported up-cycle driven by central bank de-dollarization buying, geopolitical risk aversion, and US fiscal/monetary credibility concerns, though 2026 has shown the cycle can reverse sharply (gold fell ~7-10% from H1 2026 highs to the June close). China's domestic gold production/demand backdrop is mixed: raw gold production fell in H1 2026 (safety inspections), while bar/coin investment demand rose even as jewelry demand fell.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - earnings are strongly geared to the gold price; FY2025 total profit rose 60% largely on price (gold +65%) rather than volume (+5.9%), illustrating the operating leverage in both directions
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High (inverse) - gold is a non-yielding asset; Fed rate-cut/hike expectations were the dominant swing factor behind the 2025-2026 price volatility the company itself cites

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 revenue fell 5.6% YoY to RMB53.59bn (lower purchased-gold volumes) but net profit rose 26.2% YoY to RMB3.54bn (45% YoY ex-Donghai Securities loss) as self-produced gold price gains offset a 15.4% drop in self-produced gold sales volume

Leadership change: Chairman/legal representative Han Yaodong resigned (internal SOE reassignment, no board disagreement); Wang Chenglong (senior engineer, former deputy chief engineer) elected chairman and legal representative, effective 10 July 2026

Subsidiary SDG Capital Management agreed to sell a 14.13% Donghai Securities stake to Soochow Securities for ~RMB1.95bn, triggering an estimated RMB705m fair-value accounting loss recognized in H1 2026 results

Gold price extreme volatility: international spot ranged from a 2026 high of US$5,598/oz to a low of US$3,943/oz, closing H1 2026 around US$4,007/oz (down ~7.2% from 2025 year-end close of $4,318/oz); RMB gold underperformed further due to RMB appreciation

Domestic mine safety inspections/rectifications across China reduced H1 2026 domestic raw-material gold output by 14.6% YoY industry-wide; Shandong Gold's own mine production fell 22.7% YoY as it intensified resource-integration and safety-standardization work at Jiaojia/Xincheng/Sanshandao/Penglai, with management flagging an undetermined impact on full-year 2026 targets

Completed HK$3,901m H-share placing (136.5m new shares at HK$28.58, an 8.98% discount) for debt repayment; terminated a parallel proposed A-share issuance; controlling shareholder SDG Group did not participate, diluting its stake from 45.36% to 44.02%

FY2025 revenue +26.4% to RMB104.29bn, net profit +60.6% to RMB4.74bn, operating cash flow +61% to RMB21.49bn, as gold averaged a record year (int'l spot +65% to $4,318/oz close); basic EPS RMB0.94 vs RMB0.57

Company proposed (July 2025) and then implemented (from Q1 2025/FY2025 reporting) a switch from IFRS to PRC China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/CASBE) for its consolidated financial reports, together with termination of the separate H-share IFRS auditor reappointment — a reporting-basis continuity break that complicates direct year-on-year comparison with pre-2025 IFRS-basis figures

Overseas mine production (Veladero, Argentina; Cardinal/Namdini, Ghana) rose 60.2% YoY to 12.58 tonnes, ~14% of total group gold output, while construction began on Osino's Twin Hills project in Namibia (targeted first production H1 2027)

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (published March 2026) and H1 2026 Interim Report

items.target: Qualitative only - 'stabilizing existing stock, expanding increments, curbing decrements'; no numeric 2026 gold production tonnage target disclosed
items.notes: Management explicitly states forward statements 'do not constitute a commitment to achieve production targets'; H1 2026 results already show a 22.7% YoY decline in mine gold production due to safety-driven resource integration work, with full-year impact 'not yet determined'

items.target: Expected to obtain approval by end of September 2026
items.notes: From the H1 2026 interim report; approval timing for capacity expansion, not yet confirmed as obtained in the extracted filings

items.metric: Twin Hills Gold Project (Osino, Namibia) first production
items.notes: Construction (access roads, processing plant, tailings facility) underway as of H1 2026; equipment installation and open-pit stripping in progress

items.target: Continuing to increase; FY2025 full-year payout 38.63% of net profit to ordinary shareholders (up from FY2024's ~31-40%); H1 2026 interim dividend was 34.84% of H1 net profit
items.notes: Company has a stated 'Improving Quality, Enhancing Efficiency and Prioritizing Returns' action plan and has moved toward normalized semi-annual dividends

items.metric: Cost control / cash cost per gram
items.target: Qualitative target to lower cash cost per gram of gold via 'five rates/five fees' optimization
items.notes: No numeric AISC or cash-cost guidance disclosed in the extracted filings; management explicitly flags rising costs from increasing mine depth and the shift from outsourced to self-operated construction as offsetting headwinds

guidance.management_commentary: Management frames 2026 around five pillars: stable/increased production and resource replacement (both organic exploration and M&A), value creation via cost/lean management, technology ('AI+' three-year action plan), safety/environmental risk control, and shareholder returns/market value management. On the gold price, management's own H1 2026 outlook is cautiously constructive: expects prices to 'maintain relatively high levels overall' in H2 2026 supported by safe-haven and central bank demand, but flags continued volatility risk including from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's efforts to restore Fed credibility, which could temporarily dampen prices.

bull_case: Direct, largely unhedged leverage to a structurally supported gold bull market (central bank de-dollarization buying, geopolitical risk, US fiscal/monetary credibility concerns) — FY2025 profit grew 60%+ almost entirely on price

Large, high-quality reserve base (2,054 tonnes attributable) in the world's third-largest gold district, with exploration consistently replacing depletion (81 tonnes added vs. ~49 tonnes mined in FY2025)
Fast-growing, higher-margin overseas production base (Argentina, Ghana, soon Namibia) diversifying away from mature, deepening domestic mines and growing faster than the group average

Improving capital discipline and shareholder orientation: rising dividend payout ratio, normalized interim dividends, and active controlling-shareholder stake purchases signal confidence and better alignment with minority H-shareholders
Scale and vertical integration (smelting, SOE financing access) support resilience through commodity cycles relative to smaller domestic peers
bear_case: Extreme sensitivity to gold price reversals: H1 2026 already showed prices falling ~7-10% from cycle highs, and a sustained reversal (e.g., if Fed credibility is restored, dampening safe-haven demand) would hit earnings hard given operating leverage

2026 production is explicitly disrupted by safety-driven resource-integration work (-22.7% YoY mine gold output in H1 2026) with management unable to quantify the full-year impact, creating guidance and forecasting uncertainty

Reporting discontinuity: the FY2025 switch from IFRS to PRC CAS accounting breaks clean comparability with pre-2025 IFRS-basis historicals, raising execution/analytical risk for investors and the DCF/metrics pipeline alike

SOE governance overhang: leadership (chairman/legal representative) can be reassigned by state personnel policy rather than performance or shareholder input, and capital allocation (dilutive equity raises, non-core financial investments like Donghai Securities that generated a RMB705m loss) is not purely driven by minority-shareholder value maximization

Thin-margin trading/purchased-gold revenue (41% of FY2025 sales) and heavy reliance on a single exchange counterparty (Shanghai Gold Exchange, 64.5% of sales) add low-quality revenue and concentration risk beneath a headline growth number
